decisions.claim: B indicated that Saturday evening is not available for B
decisions.reason: A's 'What a pity!' in turn 3 is a direct reaction to B declining Saturday evening, making B's unavailability for Saturday an E1 inference from A's response.

decisions.claim: B indicated that Sunday is not available for B
decisions.reason: A's 'Then when do you think we could go out together?' in turn 5 presupposes that Sunday (proposed in turn 3) was also rejected by B, making B's Sunday unavailability an E1 inference.

decisions.claim: B proposed or confirmed Friday as a possible day to go out together
decisions.reason: A's 'OK. Any time on Friday will be OK with me.' in turn 7 is an acceptance response, implying B proposed Friday. The 'OK' signals B put Friday forward.

decisions.claim: B is not available to go to the cinema on Saturday evening
decisions.reason: c4 states the same fact as c1 (B unavailable Saturday evening) with identical evidence from turn 3. c1 is the more precise representative.

decisions.claim: B is not available to go out on Sunday

decisions.claim: B proposed Friday as a day they could go out together
decisions.reason: c6 is equivalent to c3 (B proposed Friday) with the same evidence from turn 7. c3 is the more complete representative.

decisions.claim: A and B are in a social relationship where they could go to the cinema together
decisions.reason: A's phrasing 'go to the cinema with me' in turn 1 presupposes an existing social relationship where joint activities are possible. This is a genuine presupposition from A's words.
